## 8. Models

<!-- models:start (generated by tools/process_models.mjs; edit outside these markers) -->

### Ink Wash (`lumenary:ink-wash`, models this process)

_From: China and Japan; when: Tang dynasty onward, Zen painting from the 14th century; works best on: Mountains, trees, flowers and calm portraits._

Sumi-e builds every tone from a few dilutions of one ink and leaves most of the paper bare. The empty space is not a gap but part of the picture, and a stroke is meant to be seen as a gesture. This treatment gives the picture a few flat washes, lets the ink bleed into damp paper, drags a dry brush across the darks and adds a red seal.

**How it is made, as the model does it:**

1. Measure the picture’s darkness, stretched and blurred, and rescale it from a lower bound that moves with the how-much-is-inked slider.
2. Multiply by the number of tone levels and let the integer part be the tone, with a smoothstep ramp up to the next tone.
3. Blur the result twice to show ink soaking sideways, and wobble the lookup a little with the bleed slider.
4. Darken the ink where it has an edge, the tide-line a drying wash leaves.
5. Remove ink with long dry-brush streaks in the dark areas, and multiply an optional red seal onto the lower right corner.

**The maths:**

$$t=K\,\operatorname{smoothstep}(l_0,\ 1,\ d),\qquad v=\min\!\Big(1,\ \frac{1.02}{K}\big(\lfloor t\rfloor+\operatorname{smoothstep}(0.55,\,1,\ t-\lfloor t\rfloor)\big)\Big),\qquad l_0=0.6-0.5\,a$$

_Flat tones with short ramps; a is the how-much-is-inked slider._ (primitives: tone-bands, soft-threshold)

$$v\ \leftarrow\ v\,\Big[1-0.62\,D\,\operatorname{smoothstep}(0.58,\,0.85,\ \sigma)\,\operatorname{smoothstep}(0.35,\,0.8,\ v)\Big]$$

_Dry brush: σ is a noise stretched along the stroke direction, D the dry brush slider._ (primitives: tooth-threshold, soft-threshold)

$$C=C_{\text{paper}}\,(1-v)+C_{\text{ink}}\,v$$

_The ink concentration v mixes ink over paper._ (primitives: mix-over)

**Dials:** `amount` (How much is inked) = 55 [0 to 100]; `tones` (Layers of ink) = 4 [2 to 6]; `bleed` (Bleed) = 50 [0 to 100]; `dry` (Dry brush) = 50 [0 to 100]; `ink` (Ink) = "black" (black, indigo, sepia); `paper` (Paper) = "rice" (rice, white, tea); `seal` (Red seal) = true; `seed` (New brushwork) = 1.

**History:** Ink painting flourished in China under the Tang and Song dynasties and was carried to Japan by Zen monks, where Sesshū Tōyō (1420 to 1506) became its great master. Its tools are called the four treasures: brush, ink, paper and inkstone. The aesthetic of empty space, and of capturing the spirit of a subject in a few strokes, influenced Western painting and graphic design.
